summary: The paper measures a known rule, the single-algorithm cross-validated filter (fit logistic regression out-of-fold, drop disagreements, refit), on digits and breast cancer under symmetric noise with 5 seeds. It finds that most dropped samples are flipped, that the refit model beats plain logistic regression in most noisy cells and an untuned MLP in all of them, and that the clean-label cost is small. The scope is stated honestly, but the headline wording runs ahead of the weakest cells, the precision test uses the wrong null, and the MLP win carries more weight than a weak baseline can bear. The reviser cannot run new experiments, so most fixes are narrower claims, re-analysis of existing per-seed data, and stated limitations.

required_changes.change: Use one scoped claim about the gain over logistic regression in the abstract, intro paragraph 4, contribution 2 and the Sec. 4 opening: clear gains on digits at 20% and 40%, a gain on breast cancer at 40% with a seed sd of about 9 points and only about 22% of the loss recovered, and a non-significant gain on breast cancer at 20%. Remove 'in every noisy setting we ran' and 'all but one paired noisy run' (or name the run). Fix the Sec. 4 opening 'five of six dataset-noise cells', which does not match the tables; the filter has a significant gain over logistic regression in three of four noisy cells.
required_changes.where: abstract, Sec. 1 paragraph 4 and contributions 1-2, Sec. 4 opening, Sec. 4.2
required_changes.why: all four reviewers flag that the headline is stronger than the breast cancer cells, and the wording differs between abstract, intro and results. The ledger marks the low-noise breast cancer gain as weak and the 40% breast cancer recovery as partial.

required_changes.change: Replace the 50% null for precision. A random drop has precision equal to the realized flip rate (about 39% at the high rate, about 20% at the low rate; the paper already prints the realized rates). Report per-cell precision next to the realized noise rate and the lift over it, computed from existing per-seed results, and either drop the 'p vs 50%' column or relabel it as a test against 50%, not 'chance'. Drop the pooled 71% from the abstract and teaser, or label it 'pooled over four noisy cells' and give the per-cell range of 65 to 76%.
required_changes.where: Sec. 4 'Metrics and statistics', Sec. 4.1, Table 2 caption and column, abstract, Fig. 1 panel 2
required_changes.why: three reviewers agree the null is wrong and the pooled number mixes base rates. A correct baseline would make the precision claim stronger at 20% noise, where 65% is far above a 20% base rate. At 40% on breast cancer the lift is small, and the text should say so.

required_changes.change: Demote the MLP comparison. Label it everywhere as an untuned MLP reference (no tuning, no early stopping, no weight decay, not given the filtered data), and reword the Sec. 4.3 heading so that it says the MLP is hurt more by noisy labels. Remove 'beats an MLP in every run' from the abstract as a headline, and move the MLP contribution after the logistic regression comparison. State as a limitation that an MLP trained on the filtered set, a regularized or early-stopped MLP and a tuned-C logistic regression were not run.
required_changes.where: abstract, Sec. 1 contribution 2, Fig. 1 caption, Sec. 4.3 heading and text, Fig. 2 caption, Sec. 5
required_changes.why: all four reviewers say the untuned MLP is a weak baseline, so the 28-point gap shows that the MLP overfits noise, not that filtering is valuable. The paper already says the MLP was untuned, but the abstract and bullet give the win equal weight with logistic regression.

required_changes.change: State plainly that the rule is the 1999 single-algorithm filter and that the contribution is a measurement of its precision, recall, accuracy effect and clean-label cost on small symmetric-noise problems. Rewrite contribution 1 and the abstract as an empirical check of a known filter, not a new method. Add to the limitations that no comparison with confident learning, a majority-vote variant or a noise-aware logistic regression was run, so the paper cannot say whether thresholds or per-class counts matter.
required_changes.why: three reviewers say novelty is near zero and the nearest method is not compared. No baseline can be added, so honest framing is the fix. Sec. 2 already says the idea is Brodley and Friedl's, but the intro and bullets use method-paper language.

required_changes.change: Narrow the title, the Sec. 3 'Why' paragraph and Sec. 5 to what was tested: two near-linearly separable datasets, symmetric noise, 5 seeds. Add to the limitations that class-dependent noise, where a linear model's confusions follow the flips, is the obvious failure case, and that no experiment separates the effect of targeting flipped labels from the effect of dropping samples (random-drop and oracle-drop controls). Tie 'a simple first thing to try' to small symmetric-noise problems.
required_changes.where: title, Sec. 3 'Why disagreement marks a flipped label', Sec. 5
required_changes.why: reviewers say the title and mechanism sentence state a general result from two easy datasets, and that gains may come from regularization by subsampling, not targeting. Recall of 79% on breast cancer at 40% does not support 'finds the flipped labels' without qualification.

required_changes.change: Make the statistics statement honest and fix the cross-reference. Say that the p-values come from 5 paired seeds and about a dozen uncorrected tests, and are descriptive. Describe the trend test (paired difference of per-seed gains between 40% and 20%) in one sentence. Sec. 4.2 cites Table 2 for the non-significant breast cancer trend, but that table has no such test; state the p-values or cite the correct source. Report per-cell counts of seeds with a gain, from existing runs, in place of the pooled win counts.
required_changes.where: Sec. 4 'Metrics and statistics', Sec. 4.2, Table 2 caption
required_changes.why: reviewers flag thin statistics, no multiplicity note, an undescribed trend test and pooled win counts that treat runs as independent. The cross-reference error is confirmed in the paper.

required_changes.change: Treat the clean-label cost and the recovered share with their resolution. Say that on breast cancer one test sample is about 0.6 points (171 test samples), so a cost of 0.1 to 0.2 points is below one sample and 5 seeds cannot show equivalence. Define 'recovered share' in one sentence in Sec. 4.2, give the raw accuracy loss it divides by for each cell (from existing means), and note that it is unstable when that loss is small, or drop the column in favor of the paired gain. Merge the orphan breast cancer sentence into the clean-label paragraph.
required_changes.why: reviewers read 'costs a fraction of a point' as below test-set resolution and the recovered share as the authors' own unstable metric (22% to 78% across cells).

required_changes.change: Fill the missing setup details that can be taken from the code and existing results: argmax disagreement for 10-class digits, how multiclass flips are drawn, whether standardization is fit inside each fold, whether folds are stratified on the noisy labels, the MLP solver and scaling, and how time was measured. List as a limitation that the clean-label drops (about 3.5% on digits) are not broken down by class.
required_changes.where: Sec. 3 Procedure, Sec. 4 'Data and noise' and 'Models', Sec. 5
required_changes.why: clarity and soundness reviewers could not reproduce or judge the rule from the text; these are one-line additions.

required_changes.change: Rewrite contribution 3 as findings (clean-label cost, fit time, the unstable breast cancer cell) instead of 'an honest account'. Delete the Scriptorium pipeline sentence from Sec. 3. Cut Sec. 5 to the take-away and the limits not already given in Sec. 2 and 4, and delete the untested last line about passing the dropped set to a reviewer.
required_changes.where: Sec. 1 contribution 3, Sec. 3 last paragraph, Sec. 5
required_changes.why: three reviewers flag the pipeline sentence and the tone-based bullet, and Sec. 5 repeats earlier text. The cuts also free space in a 4-page limit.

optional_changes.change: Use the same noise labels (0/20/40%) in Table 1, Fig. 1, Fig. 2 and Table 2; draw the Fig. 1 dashed clean-accuracy line per dataset or drop it; replace the network icon for the model in Fig. 1 with a linear-classifier icon.

Check compiled length and the type size of the resized Table 1. If space is short, fold the Fig. 2 gains into Table 1 or cut the corresponding text numbers, since Fig. 2 and Table 1 show largely the same differences.
Note that the MLP seed varies with the split, so its variance mixes both sources, and keep the timing marked as indicative.
If the existing per-seed results show it, say whether the 9-point sd on breast cancer at 40% comes from seeds with higher realized noise or from recall; otherwise state the cause as unknown.

dismissed.point: Add CIFAR-10N or fashion-MNIST features, a harder dataset, or class-dependent noise experiments
dismissed.why: The reviser cannot run new experiments. The ledger fixes the study at two datasets and symmetric noise, and Sec. 5 already lists these as next steps. The narrowed title and the added limitation cover it.

dismissed.point: Run cleanlab, a C sweep, an MLP trained on the filtered set, K and C sensitivity, iterated filtering, random-drop and oracle-drop controls, and 20 or more seeds
dismissed.why: All need new runs. The ledger lists the missing baselines and ablations as limitations (no_baselines_no_scaling). The required changes turn them into narrowed claims and stated limitations.

dismissed.point: Add a noise-aware logistic regression baseline (Bootkrajang and Kaban)
dismissed.why: It needs a new method implementation. Related work already cites it, and the stated baseline limitation covers it.

dismissed.point: The paper says too little about its scope
dismissed.why: Several reviewers list the scope statements as strengths, and the paper states them in the abstract, Sec. 4 and Sec. 5. The only problem is that the headline wording is inconsistent with them.

dismissed.point: A per-class breakdown of dropped clean digits and the class balance of the kept set in the unstable breast cancer cell
dismissed.why: It would need per-sample drop records that the ledger does not list among its evidence keys. It becomes a limitation instead.
